title: Trump goes to Xi's home summit in Shenzhen
deck: China hosts APEC leaders on 18-19 November with Trump expected to attend, and Beijing will use its home advantage to push for tariff relief while Washington, Pyongyang, Moscow and Manila all try to turn the trip to their own ends.

card.headline: Trump plans to meet a stronger Xi on Xi's turf, with tariffs on the table and few deliverables so far

keyNumber.label: APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China's first time as host since 2014

forYou.line: Tariff relief is Beijing's top ask. Any announcement could land with little warning, so do not budget for it before it is signed.
Expect headline risk around 18-19 November. Treat a 'strategic stability' statement as different from a tariff cut.
A summit-friendly Beijing may soften pressure on its neighbours, but the calm may not last past the summit.
Trump says he 'may' meet Kim Jong Un on the trip. That is an option, not a plan.
This summit follows Xi's late-September Washington visit, which produced warm words and few concrete trade results.

effects.text: Beijing sets the agenda and the staging as host; tariff relief is its main goal
A Trump-Xi meeting on the margins is likely, building on Xi's September state visit to Washington
Shenzhen security and travel restrictions are likely around the dates (our estimate)
Other APEC economies (Japan, South Korea, Australia, Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines) use the summit to seek bilateral time
Beijing has a reason to look like a stable host, which may restrain or redirect coast-guard pressure on Manila before 18 November
Washington races to lock in other bilateral tariff deals, such as India's, before Shenzhen to strengthen its hand
Export-led Chinese growth (4.5% in Q3) with weak domestic demand raises the stakes of any tariff decision
Pyongyang's October launches gain bargaining value if a Trump-Kim meeting is possible
A Trump-Xi meeting becomes the nearest venue for the Trump-Xi-Putin summit on Ukraine that Moscow wants
Allies in Tokyo, Seoul, Taipei and Manila hedge if they fear a US-China deal made over their heads
A thin outcome would leave US-China tariff tension unresolved into 2027

whatHappened: China hosts the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen on 18-19 November 2026. It is Beijing's first time as host since 2014. Trump plans to attend.

The summit follows Xi's three-day state visit to Washington, which ended on 25 September. The two sides declared a 'constructive relationship of strategic stability'. They announced few concrete trade deliverables.

On 12 October Trump said he 'may' meet Kim Jong Un during his November Asia trip, according to Yonhap. North Korea fired a series of missiles in October, including submarine-launched cruise missiles on 14 October.
The South China Sea has been tense. At least six dangerous Philippine-Chinese encounters were reported between 1 and 9 October.
whyItMatters: As host, Beijing controls the agenda, the venue and the choreography. The South China Morning Post framed it as Trump facing a 'stronger Xi'. We have not read the article's detailed reasoning, so treat this as the paper's view rather than ours.
China's economy grew 4.5% in the third quarter on exports while domestic demand stayed weak. Tariff relief matters more to Beijing when exports are carrying the economy.

The trip bundles several crises. A Trump-Xi meeting touches the tariff war. A possible Kim meeting touches nuclear diplomacy. Putin wants a three-way summit on Ukraine. Manila is watching for any easing at sea.
The US midterm elections come on 3 November, two weeks before the summit. Trump wants tariff deals he can point to, and Xi knows it.

winners.why: Hosting gives control of the stage and the narrative, and an export-led economy gives a reason to push for tariff relief.
The mere possibility of a Trump meeting raises the value of his October launches as bargaining chips.
A Trump-Xi meeting is the nearest venue for the summit he has proposed, while he still refuses to meet Zelensky.

losers.who: Manila and other South China Sea claimants
losers.why: If Washington and Beijing prioritise a summit-friendly deal, claimants fear their disputes get sidelined.
A summit on Ukraine without Kyiv in the room would sideline Ukrainian priorities.
Taiwan takes part in APEC under the name Chinese Taipei, and a Chinese host makes its position awkward. A US-China warming adds to its worries about being traded away.
The September summit produced few trade deliverables, so a repeat is a real possibility.

whatsNext: 20-21 October: Rubio meets India's foreign minister in Mumbai and visits the Jamnagar refinery. This is a stop in the push for tariff deals before Shenzhen.
Early to mid November: expect Beijing and Washington to leak or float possible deliverables.
18-19 November: APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen. Watch for a Trump-Xi bilateral and any Kim meeting.

predict.question: Before you read the scenarios: what is the most likely outcome of Trump's Shenzhen trip?
options: A broad tariff-relief package announced with Xi
Warm words and a modest, partial deal
A summit with no tangible trade outcome
Trump skips or cuts short the trip
predict.explanation: Our base case, at about 45%, is a modest, partial outcome: a Trump-Xi meeting, some limited trade steps and fresh 'strategic stability' language. September's visit gave few deliverables, which argues against a big package. A thin outcome with almost nothing concrete is our second path, at about 30%.

timeline.title: China last hosts APEC, in Beijing
timeline.detail: Shenzhen 2026 is China's first turn as host since then.

timeline.title: US-India framework cuts tariffs
timeline.detail: The February 2026 framework cut the US reciprocal tariff on Indian goods from 25% to 18% and removed a separate 25% penalty tied to Russian oil. The first tranche is still in legal drafting. The day in February is approximate.

timeline.title: Xi's three-day state visit to Washington ends
timeline.detail: The two sides declare a 'constructive relationship of strategic stability'. Few concrete trade deliverables are announced.

timeline.title: SCMP argues Trump will face a stronger Xi in Shenzhen
timeline.detail: The analysis sets expectations that Beijing arrives as host with the upper hand.

timeline.title: South China Sea incidents begin to spike
timeline.detail: At least six dangerous Philippine-Chinese encounters are reported between 1 and 9 October, including a PLA J-16 closing on a Philippine Cessna on 3 October.

timeline.title: North Korea launches a hypersonic intermediate-range missile
timeline.detail: The first in a month of launches that includes two ballistic missiles on 12 October.

timeline.title: Trump says he 'may' meet Kim Jong Un on the Asia trip
timeline.detail: He made the remark as North Korea's launches continued. Yonhap reported it the next day.

timeline.title: North Korea tests submarine-launched cruise missiles
timeline.detail: Two types, including a Pulhwasal-3-31, its first reported sub-launched cruise test since January 2024.

timeline.title: Rubio in Mumbai for India trade talks
timeline.detail: Scheduled meeting with India's external affairs minister, followed by a Jamnagar refinery visit on 21 October.

timeline.title: US midterm elections
timeline.detail: Two weeks before Shenzhen. Domestic politics shape what Trump wants to announce.

timeline.title: APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting opens in Shenzhen
timeline.detail: Two-day summit hosted by Beijing; Trump plans to attend.

causes.name: US-China tariff contest
causes.detail: Both governments want to manage trade tension without appearing to concede, which produces warm statements with thin deliverables.

causes.name: Export dependence in China
causes.detail: Q3 growth of 4.5% came from an export surge while domestic demand stayed weak, so US tariffs matter more to Beijing.

causes.name: APEC rotation
causes.detail: China's turn to host came round again after 2014, giving Beijing the venue and agenda control.

causes.name: Xi's state visit to Washington
causes.detail: Ended 25 September with a 'strategic stability' label but few concrete trade results, leaving the work for Shenzhen.

causes.name: Trump's plan to attend
causes.detail: His attendance makes the summit a Trump-Xi event as much as an APEC meeting.

causes.name: North Korean launches
causes.detail: October launches, and Trump's 'may' meet Kim remark, add a nuclear-diplomacy track to the trip.

causes.name: South China Sea clashes
causes.detail: Beijing blocked a Sierra Madre resupply in September and clashes escalated in October, adding pressure on a stable-host image.

causes.name: Putin's summit proposal
causes.detail: Moscow wants a Trump-Xi-Putin meeting on Ukraine, and Shenzhen is the nearest place for the first two to meet.

causes.name: Pre-midterm tariff push
causes.detail: The US is trying to close bilateral tariff deals, such as India's, before the summit.

stakeholders.name: Xi Jinping
stakeholders.wants: Tariff relief and a stable-relationship headline without conceding on core issues
stakeholders.leverage: Control of the agenda and venue; export-led growth that makes China's market and supply chains hard to ignore
stakeholders.likelyMove: Stage a warm summit, offer limited trade steps, and press for tariff relief

stakeholders.name: Donald Trump
stakeholders.wants: Visible trade wins and a diplomatic show ahead of and after the midterms
stakeholders.leverage: US tariffs and the US market; the option of a Kim meeting
stakeholders.likelyMove: Seek a Xi meeting and announce purchases or tariff steps; leave the Kim meeting open

stakeholders.name: Kim Jong Un
stakeholders.wants: Sanctions relief and recognition from a US president on favourable terms
stakeholders.leverage: Missile launches and the unpredictability of his next test
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep testing and keep the door ajar to talks

stakeholders.name: Vladimir Putin
stakeholders.wants: A Trump-Xi-Putin summit on Ukraine without Zelensky
stakeholders.leverage: His relationship with Xi and the Ukraine war itself
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep pressing the summit idea and court both leaders

stakeholders.name: Philippine government
stakeholders.role: South China Sea claimant, US ally
stakeholders.wants: Uninterrupted resupply of Second Thomas Shoal and no deal over its head
stakeholders.leverage: Its alliance with Washington and international attention
stakeholders.likelyMove: Publicise any incidents and lobby Washington before Shenzhen

stakeholders.name: Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and other APEC members
stakeholders.role: Allies and economies caught in the middle
stakeholders.wants: Bilateral time with both leaders and no surprise US-China bargain
stakeholders.leverage: Trade and security ties with both powers
stakeholders.likelyMove: Seek meetings on the margins and hedge

sectors.why: Tariff relief would help most, but its absence would leave export-led growth exposed.
They gain if tariff relief is real and lose from renewed tariff threats.

sectors.sector: Shipping and logistics in the South China Sea
sectors.why: Restraint before the summit helps routes, but incidents could return afterwards.
North Korean launches and South China Sea clashes sustain demand for regional defence spending.
Summit traffic helps but security restrictions may reduce normal business (our estimate).
Headline risk around 18-19 November cuts both ways depending on the deliverables.

dailyLife.effect: A tariff-relief announcement would ease costs for US importers over months, not days. A failed summit leaves current tariffs in place.
Expect road closures and tighter security around the summit dates; we estimate this rather than cite it.
The India talks tie US waivers on Russian-energy sanctions to trade, so oil-market sentiment may move with the news.
More missile tests or sea incidents are plausible in the weeks before the summit.

scenarios.name: Modest partial deal
scenarios.looksLike: Trump and Xi meet, repeat 'strategic stability', and announce limited steps such as some purchases or targeted tariff adjustments.
signposts: Leaks of a draft joint statement in early November
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Markets get a brief relief rally; allies see a transactional approach and keep hedging.

scenarios.name: Thin outcome
scenarios.looksLike: A cordial meeting with few concrete trade outcomes, as after the September visit, and tariff relief deferred.
signposts: No working-level trade talks before the summit
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Trade friction continues into 2027; Beijing keeps using export growth to cushion weak demand.

scenarios.name: Broad breakthrough
scenarios.looksLike: A package that includes significant tariff relief, large purchases and a joint line on some regional issues.
signposts: Senior trade officials meeting in early November
Public hints from both leaders of a big announcement
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Sharp market reaction; allies worry about US-China bargains made over their heads.

scenarios.name: Derailed trip
scenarios.looksLike: Trump cancels, shortens or downgrades his attendance, or a crisis in the South China Sea or on the Korean peninsula overshadows the summit.
signposts: A serious incident with casualties at sea
A nuclear or long-range missile test
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Heightened regional tension and a loss of face for the Chinese host.

predictions.text: Trump attends the Shenzhen summit in person and holds a bilateral meeting with Xi (probability 0.8).
The meeting produces a announced tariff reduction by either side that is concrete rather than just a pledge to talk (probability 0.35).
Trump meets Kim Jong Un face to face during the Asia trip (probability 0.12).
Trump, Xi and Putin do not hold a three-way meeting in Shenzhen (probability 0.93).
At least one further dangerous Philippine-Chinese encounter is publicly reported between 1 and 17 November (probability 0.75).

actions: Do not plan around tariff relief until it is written into an official notice.
Build scenarios for both a relief announcement and a deferral, and decide your trigger points in advance.
Check travel plans and site security if you have staff or events in Shenzhen on 18-19 November.
Expect headline-driven moves around 18-19 November and size positions accordingly.
Separate 'strategic stability' language from signed trade measures.
Watch North Korean and South China Sea news as event risk for the same dates.
Do not expect shop prices to drop quickly even if a deal is announced.
Check travel advisories if you plan to visit Shenzhen or nearby routes in mid-November.
Allies should seek bilateral time on the margins and pre-clear red lines with Washington.
Keep communication lines with Beijing open on South China Sea incidents before the summit.
Prepare contingency language in case a Kim meeting becomes real at short notice.

analogues.event: Trump-Xi meeting in Busan on the sidelines of APEC
analogues.whatFollowed: From general knowledge: a one-year tariff and rare-earth truce was reported. We have not checked its detailed terms, so treat this as context rather than fact for planning.
China as host used the summit for a showpiece US-China announcement on climate; a precedent for Beijing staging a deliverable.
The meeting ended without a deal, a warning that a headline meeting can fail.
A first meeting produced warm words and few concrete steps, a template for symbolism over substance.

watch.title: Rubio in Mumbai for India trade talks
watch.why: Shows whether Washington can close bilateral deals before Shenzhen; India's first tranche is still in legal drafting.

watch.title: US midterm elections
watch.why: The result shapes Trump's domestic appetite for a trade announcement two weeks later.

watch.title: Possible expiry of the Busan truce (approximate, our recollection)
watch.why: If the one-year arrangement from October 2025 lapses around this time, it will pressure both sides to deliver in Shenzhen. Verify before relying on it.

watch.title: APEC leaders' meeting opens in Shenzhen
watch.why: First day of the summit and the likely window for a Trump-Xi meeting.

watch.title: APEC summit closes
watch.why: Any leaders' declaration, joint statement or deal announcement is likely by now.

watch.title: North Korean launches
watch.why: A longer-range or nuclear test would make a Kim meeting politically harder for Trump.

watch.title: South China Sea incidents
watch.why: A sharp drop before the summit would suggest Beijing is restraining its coast guard; a spike would suggest it is not.

confidence.note: Given in the event record and consistent with the SCMP headline.
The event record says he plans to; plans can change and we have not seen a White House confirmation.

confidence.claim: Trump may meet Kim Jong Un
confidence.note: Trump said he 'may'; this is an option, not a scheduled meeting.

confidence.claim: Tariff relief is Beijing's top summit goal
confidence.note: Stated in the event record and linked to the China Q3 growth event; we did not read the SCMP article's full reasoning.

confidence.claim: The Busan truce of October 2025 and its timing
confidence.note: From general knowledge, no source cited; included only as context and flagged as unverified.
Author judgement, not a sourced forecast; graded as events resolve.

evidence.method: Drafted from the two listed sources, their headlines, the event summary, and the briefs of connected events. We did not read the full text of either article, so the SCMP piece is used only for its headline framing. Background such as the Busan truce, Taiwan's APEC name, the 3 November US midterms and the 2014 APEC precedent comes from general knowledge and is marked as such where it appears. Scenario probabilities and prediction odds are estimates.
